summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with end-stage renal disease, diabetes, and a history of DVT, was admitted from a skilled nursing facility for hypotension and significant bleeding from a right thigh wound. Her INR was critically elevated at 7.7 due to warfarin therapy, contributing to hemorrhagic shock. She received multiple blood transfusions, vitamin K, and reversal agents. During her ICU stay, she was aggressively ultrafiltered due to volume overload. Blood cultures revealed viridans streptococci, prompting a two-week course of vancomycin, though repeat cultures were negative and imaging ruled out endocarditis or abscess. A tunneled dialysis catheter was placed after removal of a malfunctioning line, with venography showing patent central veins. Wound care was optimized, and anticoagulation was restarted with warfarin, bridged with heparin. She stabilized, transitioned to the medical floor, and was discharged to extended care with plans for ongoing dialysis, wound management, and INR monitoring.
